newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan to boost staff in 1998/99.
newsitem.headline: Nissan to boost staff in 1998/99.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Wednesday it was planning to hire a total of 900 people, including 300 new university graduates, in the year starting April 1998.
Nissan, Japan's second biggest carmaker, is scheduled to hire a total of 146 people in 1997/98.

Nissan decided to boost recruitment in 1998/99 in order to strengthen its production and sales divisions, a spokeswoman said. Nissan's total employment stood at 41,900 as of September 1996, down from a peak of 56,900 in 1991.
For the last several years, Nissan and other Japanese carmakers have reduced their workforces by cutting the number of new recruits and by not replacing workers who had retired.
